snippet.textDisplay:
This is hard work on families. I’ve helped and still help families decide which is right for them. I help not decide for them. I empower them with the information and knowledge needed to evaluate their own situations and resources (and yes you and your siblings time energy etc are resources) so THEY can choose what’s best for them. I’m the one who can take the emotions out of it and have the real conversations with them and get them thinking long term as to what they can withstand and what they cannot. It’s hard to watch your parent with dementia progress. But the decisions made have to be done in love and with the facts. The lady doesn’t love her mom any less. She knows what she and her family is able and unable to provide 24/7 52/365. Her mom being placed allows her to be a daughter and love on her mom without being stressed and her mom and everyone is safe and happy. Dementia is SCARY for both the person facing it and their families. So keep your negative comments to yourself. Her mom is clean, well cared for, loved, fed, and she spends time with her mother. She also has time for her own self care. All VERY important!

Thank you for sharing your story with all of us and keep on keeping on!

snippet.textDisplay: I cared for an ALZ grandma as a middle schooler. After a few years we had to find a home with professionals to care for her.  Same thing  for my dad.  I was there every day and weekend  just hanging out and having fun and bringing food and taking him for rides in the car while he was in full ALZ.  He didn’t know me but knew I was someone he was safe with.  I just wanted to be w him and give my stepmom a break during the day. After a while my stepmom said it’s time and we found a home.  Within 5 mo he was gone.  The best care is exactly what you’re doing — family care and the professionals will handle the rest ❤❤❤ I love your channel and content and approach to loving your mom❤ now I’m recently diagnosed vbFTD and I’ll need a family caretaker, like Norma ❤

snippet.textDisplay: Friend forget these people with so much to say until they go through it themselves alone. I used to cry every day to the point I thought I was going crazy. You did the right thing for you!!! After taking the time to take the Alzheimer’s classes, I learned that most caregivers have a higher possibility to die before the loved one they are taking care of. Do some research before you get so quick to judge another. Your situation is not hers. I like looking at your videos and I see so much of how I bonded with my mom and it makes me reflect that I did the correct things for her that I was unable to do alone.

snippet.textDisplay: I used to be one of those "Oh, I would NEVER......." people. It was ridiculous thinking and that was before I became a caregiver.
